requirements.heading: The Disposition-Notification-To Header
requirements.text: An MDN MUST NOT itself have a Disposition-Notification-To header field.

requirements.heading: The Disposition-Notification-To Header
requirements.text: An MDN MUST NOT be generated in response to an MDN.

requirements.heading: The Disposition-Notification-To Header
requirements.text: A user agent MUST NOT issue more than one MDN on behalf of each particular recipient.

requirements.heading: The Disposition-Notification-To Header
requirements.text: User agents SHOULD leverage support in the underlying message access protocol to prevent multiple MDNs from being generated.

requirements.heading: The Disposition-Notification-To Header
requirements.text: In particular, when the user agent is accessing the message using RFC-IMAP [RFC3501], it SHOULD implement the procedures specified in RFC-IMAP-MDN [RFC3503].

requirements.heading: The Disposition-Notification-To Header
requirements.text: MDNs MUST NOT be sent automatically if the address in the Disposition-Notification-To header field differs from the address in the Return-Path header field (see RFC-MSGFMT [RFC5322]).

requirements.heading: The Disposition-Notification-To Header
requirements.text: In this case, confirmation from the user MUST be obtained, if possible.

requirements.heading: The Disposition-Notification-To Header
requirements.text: If obtaining consent is not possible (e.g., because the user is not online at the time or the client is not an interactive email client), then an MDN MUST NOT be sent.

requirements.heading: The Disposition-Notification-To Header
requirements.text: Confirmation from the user MUST be obtained (or no MDN sent) if there is no Return-Path header field in the message or if there is more than one distinct address in the Disposition-Notification-To header field.

requirements.heading: The Disposition-Notification-To Header
requirements.text: The local-part comparison SHOULD be done after performing local-part canonicalization, i.e., after removing the surrounding double-quote characters, if any, as well as any escaping "\" characters.

requirements.heading: The Disposition-Notification-To Header
requirements.text: (See RFC-MSGFMT [RFC5322] for more details.) Implementations MAY treat known domain aliases as equivalent for the purpose of comparison.

requirements.heading: The Disposition-Notification-To Header
requirements.text: Similarly, if an existing message is resent or gatewayed to a newsgroup, the agent that is resending/gatewaying SHOULD strip the Disposition-Notification-To header field.

requirements.heading: The Disposition-Notification-To Header
requirements.text: Clients that see an otherwise valid Disposition- Notification-To header field in a newsgroup message SHOULD NOT generate an MDN.

requirements.heading: The Disposition-Notification-Options Header
requirements.text: An importance of "optional" indicates that an MUA that does not understand the meaning of this disposition-notification-parameter MAY generate an MDN in response anyway, ignoring the value of the disposition-notification-parameter.

requirements.heading: The Disposition-Notification-Options Header
requirements.text: notification-parameter attribute names MUST be registered with the Internet Assigned Numbers Authority (IANA) using the "Specification Required" registration policy [RFC5226].

requirements.heading: The Original-Recipient Header Field
requirements.text: RFC-DSN-SMTP [RFC3461] is amended as follows: if the ORCPT information is available, the delivering MTA SHOULD insert an Original-Recipient header field at the beginning of the message (along with the Return-Path header field).

requirements.heading: The Original-Recipient Header Field
requirements.text: The delivering MTA MAY delete any other Original-Recipient header fields that occur in the message.

requirements.heading: Use with the Message/Partial Media Type
requirements.text: When a message is segmented into two or more message/partial fragments, the three header fields mentioned in the above paragraph SHOULD be placed in the "inner" or "enclosed" message (using the terms of RFC-MIME-MEDIA [RFC2046]).

requirements.heading: Use with the Message/Partial Media Type
requirements.text: Any occurrences of the three header fields defined here in the header fields of the initial enclosing message MUST NOT be copied to the reassembled message.

requirements.heading: Format of a Message Disposition Notification
requirements.text: However, in the case of encrypted messages requesting MDNs, if the original message or a portion thereof is returned, it MUST be in its original encrypted form.

requirements.heading: Format of a Message Disposition Notification
requirements.text: The MDN MUST be addressed (in both the message header field and the transport envelope) to the address(es) from the Disposition- Notification-To header field from the original message for which the MDN is being generated.

requirements.heading: Format of a Message Disposition Notification
requirements.text: The From header field of the MDN MUST contain the address of the person for whom the message disposition notification is being issued.

requirements.heading: Format of a Message Disposition Notification
requirements.text: The envelope sender address (i.e., SMTP "MAIL FROM") of the MDN MUST be null (<>), specifying that no Delivery Status Notification messages nor other messages indicating successful or unsuccessful delivery are to be sent in response to an MDN.

requirements.heading: Format of a Message Disposition Notification
requirements.text: A message disposition notification MUST NOT itself request an MDN.

requirements.heading: Format of a Message Disposition Notification
requirements.text: That is, it MUST NOT contain a Disposition-Notification-To header field.

requirements.heading: Format of a Message Disposition Notification
requirements.text: The Message-ID header field (if present) for an MDN MUST be different from the Message-ID of the message for which the MDN is being issued.

requirements.heading: The Message/Disposition-Notification Media Type
requirements.text: Encoding considerations: "7bit" encoding is sufficient and MUST be used to maintain readability when viewed by non-MIME mail readers.

requirements.heading: The Reporting-UA Field
requirements.text: An MUA SHOULD send a "Reporting-UA" field unless specifically configured not to do so.

requirements.heading: The Reporting-UA Field
requirements.text: A reporting MUA SHOULD limit generated product identifiers to what is necessary to identify the product; a sender MUST NOT generate advertising or other nonessential information within the product identifier.

requirements.heading: The Reporting-UA Field
requirements.text: A reporting MUA SHOULD NOT generate a "Reporting-UA" field containing needlessly fine-grained detail and SHOULD limit the addition of subproducts by third parties.

requirements.heading: The MDN-Gateway Field
requirements.text: This field MUST appear in any MDN that was translated by a gateway from a foreign system into MDN format and MUST NOT appear otherwise.

requirements.heading: Original-Recipient Field
requirements.text: If there is an Original-Recipient header field in the message, or if information about the original recipient is reliably available some other way, then the Original-Recipient field MUST be included.

requirements.heading: Original-Recipient Field
requirements.text: Otherwise, the Original-Recipient field MUST NOT be included.

requirements.heading: Final-Recipient Field
requirements.text: This field MUST be present.

requirements.heading: Final-Recipient Field
requirements.text: The generic-address subfield of the Final-Recipient field SHOULD contain the mailbox address of the recipient (which will be the same as the From header field of the MDN) as it was when the MDN was generated by the MUA.

requirements.heading: Final-Recipient Field
requirements.text: Since mailbox addresses (including those used in the Internet) may be case sensitive, the case of alphabetic characters in the address MUST be preserved.

requirements.heading: Original-Message-ID Field
requirements.text: This field MUST be present if and only if the original message contained a Message-ID header field.

requirements.heading: Disposition Modes
requirements.text: (This might include the case when the user has manually configured her MUA to automatically respond to valid MDN requests.) Unless prescribed otherwise in a particular mail environment, in order to preserve the user's privacy, this MUST be the default for MUAs.

requirements.heading: Disposition Modes
requirements.text: One or the other MUST be specified.

requirements.heading: Disposition Modes
requirements.text: Unless prescribed otherwise in a particular mail environment, in order to preserve the user's privacy, this MUST be the default for MUAs.

requirements.heading: Disposition Modifiers
requirements.text: MDN disposition value names MUST be registered with the Internet Assigned Numbers Authority (IANA) using the "Specification Required" registration policy.

requirements.heading: Disposition Modifiers
requirements.text: (See Section 10 for a registration form.) MDNs with disposition modifier names not understood by the receiving MUA MAY be silently ignored or placed in the user's mailbox without special interpretation.

requirements.heading: Disposition Modifiers
requirements.text: They MUST NOT cause any error message to be sent to the sender of the MDN.

requirements.heading: Disposition Modifiers
requirements.text: However, if a message is forwarded, a "dispatched" MDN MAY be issued for the recipient doing the forwarding and the recipient of the forwarded message may also cause an MDN to be generated.

requirements.heading: Extension-Fields
requirements.text: MDN field names MUST be registered with the Internet Assigned Numbers Authority (IANA) using the "Specification Required" registration policy.

requirements.heading: Conformance and Usage Requirements
requirements.text: MUAs and gateways MUST NOT generate the Original-Recipient field of an MDN unless the mail protocols provide the address originally specified by the sender at the time of submission.

requirements.heading: Conformance and Usage Requirements
requirements.text: Successful distribution of a message to a mailing list exploder or gateway to Usenet newsgroup SHOULD be considered the final disposition of the message.

requirements.heading: Conformance and Usage Requirements
requirements.text: A mailing list exploder MAY issue an MDN with a disposition type of "processed" and disposition modes of "automatic-action" and "MDN-sent-automatically" indicating that the message has been forwarded to the list.

requirements.heading: Mail Bombing
requirements.text: For that reason, MDN's SHOULD NOT be sent automatically where the Disposition-Notification-To address is different from the SMTP "MAIL FROM" address (which is carried in the Return-Path header field).

requirements.heading: Gatewaying from Other Mail Systems to MDNs
requirements.text: For MDNs produced from foreign disposition notifications, the name of the gateway MUST appear in the MDN-Gateway field of the MDN.

requirements.heading: IANA Considerations
requirements.text: IANA MAY reject registrations because of incomplete registration forms or incomplete specifications.
